picked.title: An Empirical Study of Reinforcement Learning for Keypoint Positioning of Deformable Linear Objects
picked.summary: Deformable linear object (DLO) manipulation is challenging because high-dimensional configurations, nonlinear contact dynamics, and diverse material and geometric properties produce a broad range of object responses that are both difficult to model and data-intensive to learn. This work studies reinforcement learning for planar manipulation of a one-end-grasped DLO, focusing on training efficiency, observation design, robustness, and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. We compare three Proximal Policy Optimization training stacks and find that the GPU-parallel MuJoCo Playground stack enables faster convergence and more consistent performance than CPU-based alternatives under the same wall-clock budget. Relative keypoint observations and an asymmetric actor-critic formulation further improve learning efficiency. Policies trained with observation noise, delay, domain randomization, and disturbances achieve simulation success rates of 96.4% for single-point tracking, 98.0% for disturbance recovery, and 88.8% for two-point tracking. Using markerless RGB-D keypoint estimation, the policies transfer without real-world fine-tuning, succeeding in 9/10, 10/10, and 8/10 physical trials, respectively.

picked.title: AffectiveVLA: Safe and Intent-Aware VLA Control for Human-Humanoid Social Interaction
picked.summary: Social touch interactions, such as handshakes, fist bumps, and hugs, require humanoid robots to infer human intent, generate contact-rich motions, and maintain safe physical contact. We present AffectiveVLA, an intent-gated Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pipeline deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. A lightweight RGB-based model recognizes interaction intent from two onboard cameras and converts it into a language prompt for the VLA policy. Low-confidence predictions suppress motion execution, reducing unintended activations. During physical contact, interaction-specific compliance profiles adjust arm impedance, while an independent voice-triggered mechanism initiates a latched safe-stop procedure. Using VR teleoperation, we collected approximately 1,300 multimodal interaction episodes and fine-tuned four VLA models: GR00T, RLDX-1, Being-H0.5, and UnifoLM-VLA-0. On-robot evaluation identifies GR00T as the best-performing standalone model. Integrating intent recognition increases its macro-F1 score from 0.75 to 0.90, while the intent model achieves a p95 inference latency of 6.27 ms. These results demonstrate that explicit intent gating improves the reliability of VLA-based social interaction without compromising real-time operation.

picked.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
picked.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.

picked.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
picked.summary: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

picked.title: MuJoCo 4.0.0
picked.summary: Version 4.0.0 (November 6, 2026) Significant new features 89daf8d19 Added the speculative enable flag for speculative contacts to prevent fast-moving convex geoms from tunneling through thin obstacles within a single timestep. On the right, one step of conservative advancement between two rotating boxes. See model/speculative/ for examples. Added elasto-plasticity, with stateful plastic deformation stored in mjData.plastic ( mjSTATE_PLASTIC ): e140c026f Ideal elasto-plasticity for joint ( springyield ) and tendon ( spatial , fixed ) springs (left). 0c0f63b3f , c39fe6f02 , e3bd72742 , 7cb32488b Continuum elasto-plasticity ( yield ) for 2D and 3D flexes , with separate stretching and bending yield strains for 2D shells, volumetric-deviatoric (von Mises $J_2$ ) stretching and 2D shell bending return mapping (right). See model/plastic/ for examples. abaf8d518 Split the Python distribution into mujoco-core (minimal bindings and C library depending only on numpy ), mujoco-studio (Studio and Filament renderer bindings), and mujoco (default package installing both). When upgrading from a pre-split mujoco installation with pip , uninstall first ( pip uninstall -y mujoco && pip install mujoco ) or run pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps mujoco mujoco-core mujoco-studio after upgrading so pip does not remove files moved to mujoco-core . To switch an existing mujoco installation to core-only, run pip uninstall -y mujoco mujoco-studio && pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps mujoco-core . Note Updated documentation for the split Python packages ( mujoco , mujoco-core , mujoco-studio ) and prebuilt OpenUSD wheels ( mujoco-usd / mujoco[usd] ) landed shortly after the 4.0.0 release ( 39ddbb61a ). Please refer to the latest docs for Python bindings and OpenUSD rather than stable or 4.0.0 .
